label: o_control_errorfree
mechanism: ERROR-FREE control; recorded equals true
why: A negative control: audit finds nothing. Clean electronic import from the analyser.

label: o_noise_noclusters
mechanism: Row assay noise; no cluster structure at all
why: Imprecision of a single central lab: sites carry no information about value or error.

label: o_easy_large
mechanism: 150 sites, mild noise, small offsets
why: A well-run network with modest imprecision. Nothing should struggle here.

label: o_pairs_k150
mechanism: Two rows per cluster, site offsets and noise
why: Paired records such as mother-infant or two-visit audits: many clusters, each tiny.

label: o_offset_x_within
mechanism: Large site offsets, covariate varies only within site
why: Within-site allocation (a shift, a ward, a sex-balanced sample): site bias is large but orthogonal to the covariate.

label: o_offset_x_site
mechanism: Binary site-level covariate, site offset dominates
why: Facility ownership against a facility-calibrated value. Clustering dominates; effective sample is the 40 sites.

label: o_offset_few_unbal
mechanism: 20 sites, hospitals and posts, heavy-tailed offsets
why: A small district network: a few big hospitals hold most rows, and one odd lab can sit far off.

label: o_calib_slope
mechanism: Site calibration slope, error grows with the value
why: Glucose analysers drift in percent, so high readings carry large site-shared error.

label: o_regress_to_mean
mechanism: Row-level compression toward the mean
why: Self-report and recall: people and staff understate extremes, so error depends on the value.

label: o_bias_by_x
mechanism: Common bias depending on the covariate, three strata
why: Busier or older-patient clinics under-record systematically, directly bending the slope.

label: o_site_bias_by_x
mechanism: Site-specific bias slope on the covariate
why: One clinic misreads a subgroup and another the opposite: the error slope varies by site, zero on average.

label: o_hetero_value
mechanism: Noise grows with distance from the mean, sloppy sites
why: Point-of-care meters lose precision at extreme readings, and some sites handle them worse.

label: o_digit_preference
mechanism: Rounding to 10 at most sites, unbalanced sizes
why: Terminal-digit preference in manual blood pressure is widely seen; some sites use automated cuffs.

label: o_decimal_slip
mechanism: Sparse 10-fold slips, clumped by site
why: Decimal point errors in keyed lab values: rare, enormous, and concentrated with certain clerks.

label: o_unit_mixup_sites
mechanism: Whole sites report in another unit
why: A site reports mmol/L in an mg/dL field. Every row at that site is off by 18-fold, and few sites do it.

label: o_lod_floor
mechanism: Limit-of-detection floor, binary covariate
why: Viral load below the assay limit is reported at the limit: value-dependent, one-sided error.

label: o_counts_underreport
mechanism: Register counts thinned by site completeness
why: Monthly totals: events go missing from the summary form at a rate specific to the facility.

label: o_counts_inflate_pay
mechanism: Sites paid by volume inflate, more at high covariate
why: Performance-based financing rewards reported volume, and some facilities respond.

label: o_claims_lognormal
mechanism: Heavy-tailed costs with percent errors by biller
why: Claim amounts are long-tailed and billers vary in inflating them. Hard: a few rows drive everything.

label: o_heavy_t3_k30
mechanism: t3 true values and t3 errors at both levels, 30 sites
why: Mixed populations plus occasional bad runs give rare extremes at both patient and site level.

label: o_contextual
mechanism: Contextual effect of site covariate mean
why: Case mix: a site's composition moves everyone there (referral pattern), so between and within slopes differ.

label: o_size_informative
mechanism: Size linked to true value, covariate and error
why: Big hospitals have sicker patients, different values and better records than small posts.

label: o_random_slope_k25
mechanism: Covariate effect varies by site, 25 sites
why: A within-site allocation whose effect differs by local practice, so the row-level slope is a site average.

label: o_strata_one_bad
mechanism: One small stratum bad and oversampled in the audit
why: Private facilities outside the support system err more, and auditors deliberately sample more of them.

label: o_strata_slopes
mechanism: Covariate slope differs by stratum
why: Urban and rural facilities differ in the covariate's effect, so the pooled slope is a weighted average.

label: o_copy_forward
mechanism: Copy-forward of the line above, 30 rows per site
why: Register fatigue: a clerk repeats the previous entry, so errors are bounded in size but look real.

label: o_fabricated_sites
mechanism: A few sites fabricate believable values
why: Desk-filled forms at remote sites: right range, no link to the patient.

label: o_threshold_gaming
mechanism: Values nudged above a payment threshold at some sites
why: Pay-for-performance targets: readings just below the cut are pushed over it, creating a heap.

label: o_zero_for_blank
mechanism: Blanks keyed as zero, rate clumped by site
why: Registers with a mandatory field: an untested patient becomes 0. Common in aggregate and lab data.

label: o_drift_within_run
mechanism: Site-specific drift across rows of a run
why: Reagent lots and calibrations age through a run, at site-specific rates, unrelated to who is tested.

label: o_tiny_k20_n3
mechanism: 20 sites of 3 rows, skewed covariate
why: A small spot-check study. Few rows mean little to learn from and much to fear from any one site.

label: o_quadratic_truth
mechanism: True value curved in a skewed covariate
why: Biomarkers often move nonlinearly with age or load, so OLS's slope is only a projection.

label: o_two_tier_k150
mechanism: 150 sites, many posts and few hospitals, site offsets
why: A national network: many clusters overall, yet most rows sit in a small share of them.

label: p_control_errorfree
mechanism: ERROR-FREE control; recorded equals true
why: A negative control for the predictor role. Clean electronic import.

label: p_noise_noclusters
mechanism: Classical row noise; no cluster structure at all
why: One central lab, independent patients, and a modest assay imprecision.

label: p_easy_large
mechanism: 150 sites, mild noise
why: A large, well-run network with reliable data. Nothing should struggle here.

label: p_low_reliability
mechanism: Row noise as large as the true variation, unbalanced sizes
why: Single spot measures of a variable quantity, such as one blood pressure reading for a habitual level.

label: p_offset_mixed
mechanism: Site offset plus row noise at similar scale
why: A multi-lab network: each lab has its own offset and its own imprecision.

label: p_site_dominant
mechanism: True value and error both nearly all between sites
why: Value set by site (water source, altitude, local protocol) and the error too. Clustering dominates.

label: p_offset_few_unbal
mechanism: 20 sites, hospitals and posts, heavy-tailed site effects
why: A small network where one big hospital sets most of the data and the audit may miss it.

label: p_calib_slope
mechanism: Site calibration slope on the predictor
why: Percent-off analysers feeding a regression: the size of the error scales with the value.

label: p_berkson_nominal
mechanism: Berkson: the register holds a nominal assigned value
why: Prescribed dose or a kit's lot value is recorded and the actual value scatters around it.

label: p_differential_outcome
mechanism: Error depends on the outcome
why: Unblinded recording: a patient who did badly gets a value written with that in mind.

label: p_shared_site_quality
mechanism: Site quality moves both outcome and recording bias
why: Well-run facilities get better outcomes and keep different records, so error links to the site's outcome residual.

label: p_bias_by_x
mechanism: Bias depending on the covariate, two strata
why: Older or sicker patients are measured differently, so the error is tied to another regressor.

label: p_decimal_slip
mechanism: Sparse 10-fold slips on the predictor
why: A few enormous keyed values have huge leverage when the value is a regressor.

label: p_lod_floor
mechanism: Limit-of-detection floor on the predictor
why: A censored viral load is used as an exposure, a common practice with a value-dependent error.

label: p_digit_preference
mechanism: Rounding to 10 at most sites
why: Hand-rounded blood pressure used as an exposure. Errors are bounded but tied to the value.

label: p_contextual_truth
mechanism: Outcome depends on site mean of the true value
why: Peer or environmental effect: site average matters beyond the individual's value, so OLS mixes both.

label: p_log_dose
mechanism: Lognormal predictor, outcome linear in its log
why: Biomarkers such as ferritin act on a log scale but are analysed raw, so the target is a projection.

label: p_threshold_gaming
mechanism: Outcome steps at a threshold that recording games
why: A clinical cut drives care and hence outcomes, and staff push values over that same cut.

label: p_heavy_t3_k30
mechanism: t3 throughout: truth, outcome and errors, 30 sites
why: Outliers everywhere, in values and in outcomes, with few sites to average them away.

label: p_size_informative
mechanism: Size linked to true value, outcome, covariate and error
why: Large sites differ in everything. Which sites get audited changes what the audit looks like.

label: p_strata_one_bad
mechanism: One small stratum bad and oversampled in the audit
why: Private facilities err more, and auditors deliberately sample more of them.

label: p_random_slope_k25
mechanism: Dose response varies by site, 25 sites
why: Local care changes how the value relates to outcome, so the row-level slope is a site average.

label: p_copy_forward
mechanism: Copy-forward of the line above, 30 rows per site
why: Repeat entries unlink value from patient, while the outcome stays with the patient.

label: p_fabricated_sites
mechanism: A few sites fabricate believable values
why: Plausible desk-filled values, unrelated to the patient, while outcomes come from another system.

label: p_counts_underreport
mechanism: Counts thinned by site completeness
why: Facility volume from a register predicts an outcome, with completeness varying by site.

label: p_x_site_level
mechanism: Site-level covariate strongly tied to the true value
why: A facility attribute predicts the value, so its effect and the value's are hard to separate.

label: p_zero_for_blank
mechanism: Blanks keyed as zero, rate clumped by site
why: An untested patient recorded as 0 becomes a huge outlier when the value is a regressor.

label: p_two_tier_k150
mechanism: 150 sites, many posts and few hospitals, site offsets
why: A national network: many clusters overall, yet most rows sit in a small share of them.

label: p_tiny_k20_n3
mechanism: 20 sites of 3 rows, skewed covariate
why: A tiny spot-check. The audit sees 15 rows at the lower fraction.
